html:
The 2006 Lebanon War was a war of 34 days between Israel and Hezbollah, from July to August 2006. It began when Hezbollah fighters crossed the border, killed several Israeli soldiers and captured two.

Israel answered with air strikes across Lebanon, bombing roads, bridges, Beirut's airport and the southern suburbs of Beirut, and later sent troops into the south. Hezbollah fired thousands of rockets into northern Israel. More than a thousand Lebanese were killed, most of them civilians, and about 160 Israelis.

A UN resolution ended the fighting and sent more peacekeepers to the south. Hezbollah, which had survived, claimed victory, and its standing in Lebanon and the Arab world rose. Compare Israel's earlier war in Lebanon in 1982.
sum: The 2006 Lebanon War was a war of 34 days between Israel and Hezbollah, from July to August 2006. It began when Hezbollah fighters crossed the border, killed several Israeli soldiers and captured two.
